claim: The app or browser generates the request id and persists it locally before submitting, so a client restart mid-flight is covered.

title: Split the release across two people at the validation boundary
claim: A Friday manager cuts the changelog and pushes; a different Monday manager validates and triggers the release. When version compatibility is implicated, one additional reviewer's only job is finding upgrade bugs.

title: Two-tier documentation with an ingest-optimized lane
claim: User docs are structured as tutorial, guide, reference plus a concepts tier for the why; internal docs deliberately have no style requirement because "it's more important to have something documented", with a stated compaction promise.

title: Assign, do not request, review
claim: Review is level-triggered rather than edge-triggered, with exactly one reviewer to avoid the bystander effect, and the author picks the reviewer.

title: Exhaustive generation of bounded value sequences
claim: Instead of random fuzzing, exhaustively generate bounded value sequences - about a hundred dependency-free lines.

title: Speaker identity and language are separable inputs
claim: Four seconds of Chinese reference audio generated English in that voice, across a claimed fifty languages, so speaker identity and output language are independent inputs.

title: Configuration-smell prevalence across 100 repositories
claim: Across 100 popular repositories: lint leakage 62%, context bloat 42%, skill leakage 35%, and most files carried at least one smell.

title: The recording is the authorship verification
claim: Hiring runs on a full-screen recording of the candidate building a feature unsupervised with no interview first, and the same artifact becomes the ongoing management signal.

title: Waterfall enrichment with value-level provenance
claim: Enrichment runs as a waterfall across providers, with provenance recorded at the level of the individual value rather than the record.

title: A source ranked first, second and Pareto-optimal at once
claim: The source claims first on one public multilingual benchmark, second on another leaderboard, and 'defines the Pareto frontier' on a third framing, all simultaneously and all plausibly true - a clean instance of the run's own landed argument appearing in the source's self-description.

title: A removed-surface guard keyed to files, not only identifiers
claim: The removed-surface guard carries both BANNED_PATTERNS and REMOVED_FILES, so a fork's removal is enforced against the files that are gone as well as against the identifiers that named them.

title: The routing grain is one upstream API request
claim: The routing grain is one upstream API request, because an agent turn contains many upstream calls with different characteristics (main loop versus tool result) and 'turn' already meant three things in the codebase; session state may inform the decision but not be its grain, and the notation addresses a subagent's Nth call.

title: Composite truth tables for three-valued conditions
claim: Three-valued conditions where a timeout or an unavailable provider returns null, with composite operators defined so that 'none' over an unevaluable child returns null - absence can never satisfy a negative check.

title: Classify a question before asking the human
claim: Classify a question before asking the human: codebase facts are never asked, and questions arrive one at a time.

title: Rule identity bound to prose couples the oracle to messages
claim: The oracle recovers rule identity by matching a message substring, so its rule identity is bound to prose; the ADR says 'assert the rejecting rule or category' and the tree cannot, because the validator returns strings.

title: Plan before create on an agent-facing surface
claim: An agent-facing surface pairs a side-effect-free plan call with the creating call, the skill says 'always plan before create', and install:false keeps the dry run under transport timeouts.

title: A conceptual formalism in a results position is not validation
claim: The paper presents an equation that nothing solves, no gradient touches and no search optimizes, in the slot where evidence goes, and the authors concede it is a conceptual lens.

title: A default ships with its ceiling and its escape seam named
claim: A default is published together with the ceiling it will hit and the seam through which a caller escapes it - stated in the doc comment rather than discovered when the ceiling arrives.

title: Environment-dependent defaults invert on the server
claim: The same library ships opposite defaults per environment - retry 0 and eviction never on the server side - because the lifetime and the cost of a mistake differ by execution context.

title: Publish the flag that regenerates your benchmark
claim: Publish the flag that regenerates your benchmark, not just the benchmark, so a reader can reproduce the number on their own tree.

title: Post your token usage or it does not count
claim: An adoption claim is not credible without the spend evidence behind it.

title: An issue is created after a machine-made repro, not from feedback
claim: Untrusted feedback becomes an issue only after a machine-made repro: check whether it is already fixed, dedupe, generate a clean repro, and only then create the issue - 'an issue isn't created from feedback; issues are created post feedback' - and it works for issues with clear code repros, with anything hard to reproduce going to a human.

title: N labelled prompt blocks with per-block lifetimes, for video
claim: The whole prompt is split into labelled blocks instead of one paragraph; some blocks are locked and will not change between generations, and the rest vary.

title: Durations first, narration written to each shot's word budget
claim: Shot durations are fixed first and the narration is written to the word budget each duration allows - 'each video only gives me a certain number of words to work with'.

title: One source of truth per artifact beside a legacy tracker
claim: Each artifact has exactly one source of truth chosen from repo, legacy tracker, or a linkage minimum, so a team running both systems does not have two authorities for the same object.

title: Displayed value chases true value
claim: Exponential approach applied to a jittery real signal so a stuttering data source renders as smooth progress - the bar chases the target even when the real progress is choppy.

title: Randomness is bounded, never pure
claim: Randomness in motion runs over controlled ranges rather than pure random, and the designer explicitly decides the boundary between what is controlled and what is delegated to variance.

title: Ship no launcher: put the protocol in the served page
claim: The test-runner core ships no browser launcher and no framework; the reporting protocol lives in the page it serves, so each of six automation backends is a thin adapter and the reporting path is identical across all of them.

title: Premount trades memory for frame time and stops the window releasing
claim: Mounting off-screen neighbours in frame gaps up to a deadline minus a buffer buys frame time, and when it is on the incremental-mount window stops releasing.

title: A house-style name is a style token, not a content token
claim: Naming a publication's house style in a generation prompt sets style, and treating it as a content instruction is the failure; the row was promoted from partial to real during the run.

title: Worktree isolation now accepts plain shell
claim: 2.1.257 lets worktree isolation accept plain shell, and 2.1.203 makes EnterWorktree outside .claude/worktrees/ confirm rather than refuse.

title: Settings migration filtered by the target's declared capability
claim: Only flags listed in the model's image_prompt_types_allowed survive a settings migration, and unsupported sliding-window modes migrate to queue-task modes.

title: An accelerator carries a sampler contract
claim: Guidance must drop to 1 with the accelerator engaged or output is both worse and twice as slow, and the multiplier must be re-tuned with the step count (12 steps to 0.3, 8 steps to 0.5-0.7).

title: An unrecognised override must be ignored, never honoured
claim: An unrecognised backend override is ignored rather than honoured, so a stale override cannot mask a healthy backend.

title: Capability-conditional skips decide lane membership by annotation
claim: skip_if_quick, SkipIfBeforeComputeCapabilityVersion and SkipIfBeforePyTorchVersion route tests by hardware capability and library version at the decorator, not by location.

title: An isolation boundary must publish what it does not isolate
claim: A boundary that isolates some properties and not others has to enumerate the exclusions; this is the second sighting.

title: Experiment tables overwrite by name and store completion order
claim: Experiment result tables are keyed by experiment name and overwritten in place, and rows land in completion order rather than in the requested order.

title: Dependency-free near-duplicate checker for the registry
claim: A 5-word-shingle containment check with a 30 percent document-frequency boilerplate strip and a 0.80 containment threshold detects near-duplicate pages, and would work on our own applications across a bundle.

title: Five places sources disagree as a research method
claim: A research dossier template requires the author to name the five places its sources disagree, making disagreement a deliverable rather than a nuisance.

title: Never render the mock's example data on the real surface
claim: An agent instruction file forbids shipping the mockup's example projects; the gallery renders only real upstream entries.

title: The enumeration gap is the model difference
claim: A redirect-only payment provider appears in the customer factory but not the payment factory and has no payments directory; that enumeration gap is itself the statement that its model differs.

title: Sparse snapshots diff against the previous existing row
claim: No snapshot row is written on a day with no events, so the day-over-day diff is taken against the previous existing snapshot, and the invariant is that the usage diffs sum exactly to final usage.

title: Reject the field the caller may not set
claim: A request that carries a tenant field should be rejected rather than have the field ignored, because a rejection tells you someone is testing your boundary and silence does not.

title: A dependency-free module as the shared kernel
claim: Three processes need the same chunk arithmetic and a copy in each would be free to drift, so the module imports nothing heavy at module level and the lightest consumer can reach it by bare import.

title: A listing becomes a credential-free fetch-and-render surface
claim: Icon and website-URL fields turn a server listing into a surface that fetches and renders remote content without credentials.

title: A policy authority that is neither endpoint
claim: An enterprise identity provider acts as a policy authority that is neither the client nor the server in the protocol's two-party model.

title: Discovery burden transferred on a population-ratio argument
claim: The specification moves discovery work from servers to clients, justified by the ratio of the two populations rather than by which side is better placed.

title: The replacement must be live at both ends
claim: The design record required that a replacement be live at both ends before the old form retires, and the published policy dropped the rule.

title: A deprecation that breaks the policy adopting it
claim: The dynamic client registration deprecation breaks the lifecycle policy in the very revision that adopted that policy.

title: A maintainer's procedure shipped as an in-repo skill
claim: The maintenance procedure ships as four in-repo agent skills, with the changelog declared agent-owned and not hand-editable.

title: The chunker choice is part of the chunk
claim: Which chunker produced a chunk must be recorded with it, or a re-chunk is unreproducible.

title: A derived chunk boundary costs a second ingest pass
claim: Embedding-similarity boundary detection buys coherence and pays an extra embedding pass at ingest time.

title: Dual-store consistency with no transaction
claim: The same fact lands in both the graph store and the vector store with no transaction spanning them.

title: The risk asymmetry between a constrained design and a frozen one
claim: A workaround constraining a design pre-freeze costs a worse name - bounded and known before shipping - while an unvalidated design shipped and frozen costs an unbounded amount discovered later.

title: A shipped document enumerating what the gates do not catch
claim: A shipped document enumerates what the quality gates do not catch, with a known-bypass-patterns section and a defense changelog, naming sycophancy bias, confidence-ceiling arbitrage and slow vocabulary rotation evading deduplication.

title: A profile asserting unconfirmed flags is worse than no profile
claim: Every flag in the profile was checked against the tool's own help output, because a profile that asserts flags nobody confirmed is worse than its absence.

title: Sequential record ids foreclose merging by construction
claim: Sequential record identifiers make merging impossible by construction, deliberately.

title: Validate a machine-proposed widening before storing it
claim: A remembered approval is an EXACT session+agent rule; a SIMILAR widening is proposed by the model and validated (it still matches the target, keeps its anchor, is not destructive), with the exact rule as the fallback.

title: Quiesce writers and refuse symlinked parents before restore
claim: Restore quiesces writers, mints refs/pre-restore/* in the same transaction, and refuses symlink or junction parents.

title: A unit in the type; the convenience layer fails for absolute quantities
claim: A quantity's unit is part of its type, and the convenience arithmetic layer is unsound for absolute quantities.

title: Provenance metadata from the revision, not the build event
claim: Provenance metadata is derived from the source revision rather than from the build event.

title: Additive-only bumps while experimental; consumer pins the contract SHA
claim: Bump the contract only for additive changes during the experimental phase, and the consumer's first change references the commit SHA of the contract file it implements against.

title: Co-location buys cohesion, never decoupling
claim: Regrouping immediately increases cohesion but does not automatically reduce coupling, so the move is a half-move and teams stop after step one.

title: The incumbent's per-unit distribution is a free demand signal
claim: Priority numbers are derived from per-utility monthly download counts, because the rival ships one package per function.

title: Degenerate inputs test nothing
claim: Identical union sides do not test union logic, and [1,1,1] hides bugs that [1,2,3] catches.

title: Cross-link for a reader choosing, never for one migrating
claim: A mapping page for migrating one call site must not mention its sibling, while reference docs for a reader choosing between functions must cross-link symmetrically.

title: Brand the error sentinel so it cannot pass as a value
claim: The error sentinel uses a branded symbol rather than a raw string, because raw strings pass through downstream without being caught.

title: Content reachable only through the escape hatch counts as absent
claim: A rubric's anti-gaming clause: content carried only inside the raw-markup escape hatch does not count as present.

title: Identity anchors are not only for faces
claim: Any prop that must survive a cut needs its own reference sheet.

title: An orchestrator sizes its sub-agent count to the task
claim: The orchestrator dispatched one sub-agent because the task was small.

title: An inbox of sessions awaiting the operator
claim: An inbox listing the sessions that await the operator's input.

title: Parity governs behaviour, not performance
claim: The engine acceptance bar governs behavioural parity and explicitly does not claim performance parity.

title: A regression test carries the issue id in its name
claim: Of 405 top-level test files, 37 are named for the issue they regress.

title: Two defaults on purpose for a cache-key knob
claim: A knob whose default folds into a cache key keeps the pre-wave value so a legacy config literal preserves its hash identity, while every shipped bundle sets the new one.

title: An undecidable check answers permissively in a bool
claim: match_host decides whether two handles share an isolate and sometimes cannot; the comment says it is "a bit too forgiving [...] it just returns true [...] needs to be tightened up", and the adjacent assert turns that value into an authorisation.

title: Stage work off the metered clock
claim: It helps to line everything up before you spin up the GPUs, but at this stage you have to spin them up because you need to load weights - an operating rule with an honest concession that part of the setup is irreducible on the metered clock.

title: A model-facing quality bar is one shared constant
claim: A model-facing quality bar must be one shared constant or the word drifts per surface - so that "atomic" never degrades into one shallow fact per symbol.

title: Effort and tier axes are non-monotonic per task
claim: One model gets monotonically worse with more effort, and ultra is better than max and actually cheaper - so an effort axis is not ordered per task.

title: Regenerate rather than edit in place
claim: Throwing code away and regenerating beats editing it in place, and context-preserving loops beat context-clearing ones on the one task measured.

title: Token subset invariants as ingest checks
claim: The token fields carry subset invariants that an ingest pipeline can check, rather than being accepted as independent numbers.

title: Billed over consumed, as a normative rule
claim: The conventions state normatively that a billed quantity takes precedence over a consumed one.

title: Ceiling model for structure, cheap tier for tweaks
claim: The ceiling model runs the dispatch that sets structure; a cheap tier handles tweaks and the recurring background loop.

title: Recurring agent jobs pinned to prompt, workspace, provider and model
claim: A scheduled agent job carries a pinned tuple - prompt, workspace, provider, model - as its definition.

title: Partition the vault by source class as it grows
claim: "I have one vault for my YouTube videos, one for business knowledge, one for meeting transcripts. I started to separate them out over time" - an evolution under load, with no mechanism stated.

title: Change rate, not importance, decides store-versus-fetch-live
claim: The source's context-versus-connections split is change rate: evergreen material is persisted, daily-changing material is reached at need.

title: Alphabetical order as merge-conflict control
claim: CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template both require alphabetical order; in a one-file corpus with 50 appenders that gives every insertion a deterministic position, localising conflicts instead of piling them at end-of-file.

title: A consolidation invariant that only holds in DEBUG
claim: Consolidation's metadata-equality invariant is asserted only in DEBUG builds, so the shipped binary never checks it.

title: An AOT carve-out gated by review only
claim: The AOT package carve-out is enforced by review alone, with no check that reads the project file.

title: A 20k-word human document as the machine-read eval source of truth
claim: A 20,000-word human prompt document is the machine-read source of truth for generated evals, with a per-row eligibility column whose four values do not quite account for every row.

title: Four distinct not-approved outcomes in one elicitation response
claim: The elicitation response carries four distinct not-approved outcomes rather than a single refusal.

title: A loader that skips initialization when the test proxy is set
claim: RegistryToolLoader skips all initialization when the test proxy is set, to avoid polluting recordings.

title: A prefix-key cache fallback makes CI exercise both migration roads
claim: Restore-keys restore the nearest older template and migrate it forward; the fixture is built by the upgrade road when the prefix hits and by the fresh road when nothing hits, so CI exercises both roads by accident.

title: An operator interrupt is not a crash
claim: The cleanup trap sends nothing when the signal is INT - an operator interrupt is deliberately not reported as a crash.

title: A floating-input branch may only be installed from its head
claim: Every older commit on the branch was paired with inputs that no longer exist, so installation is only valid from the branch head.

title: Sanitize at the encoder, not after stringify
claim: Egress-time Unicode sanitization as a single-point invariant, because lone surrogates reach the API as a 400.

title: Seed a hermetic environment from the live tree, never a snapshot
claim: The hermetic end-to-end environment uses an allowlist-scrubbed environment, a fresh config dir, and live-tree skill seeding by symlink - so the test measures the tree, not a snapshot of it.

title: Price an inflated numerator: logical SLOC above raw LOC
claim: LOC deflation - reporting logical SLOC and weighted commits above raw LOC, with the comparison script published.

title: Image-edit inference is deliberately local to the previous turn
claim: Only an image on the immediately preceding assistant message is reused for an image edit - never one from across intervening turns.

title: Capability is the range you can move through, not the ceiling
claim: Capability is the range of altitudes you can operate at, not the highest one you reach; retain bidirectional movement.

title: Operating range is per-domain, not per-person
claim: Switching domains resets your operating range regardless of engineering skill.

title: Output size as a property of the response contract
claim: Resolution is a response_format field rather than a top-level parameter - the request shape treats output size as a property of the response contract.

title: Extract the undisclosed funding constraint behind an investment
claim: The real driver of an investment decision is often a funding constraint nobody has stated; extract it before proposing.

title: Instruction files are not memory
claim: Human-authored static context and model-written accumulation are different families and must be kept distinct.

title: Task-state lifecycle across sessions
claim: Stale task state made later sessions confusing; the standalone question of task-state lifecycle was never opened.

title: Keep the model's own words beside the digest
claim: The model's verbatim output is retained alongside the digest computed from it, rather than being replaced by the digest.

title: A ban test that catches only the bare form
claim: The security test bans bare `exec` and nothing else, so the check passes against every non-literal route to the same capability.

title: Keyword escalation with a fixed negation list
claim: Escalation is triggered by keywords with a fixed list of negations, so the policy is exactly as good as that list is complete.

title: Authority framing on a reused answer
claim: A similarity-gated answer reuse is presented to the user with authority framing, so a cache hit above a threshold reads as a fresh authoritative answer.

title: A character allowlist that admits an exponent bomb
claim: The calculator tool guards input with a character allowlist that admits `9**9**9`, so the guard permits an expression that cannot be evaluated safely.

title: When auto-rig fails, harvest the skeleton
claim: Auto-rig failed outright, so the preset's skeleton was exported, its bones positioned on the character by hand, and automatic weights applied - the reusable artifact was the skeleton, not the rig.

title: Poly tier is chosen per part, not per asset
claim: Some parts (hair, head) go low-poly immediately while arms, legs and the general body are done high-poly, so the low-direct versus dense-and-finish choice is made per part where the golden path states it per asset.

title: Sparse reconstruction saturates, and the knee matters
claim: Faithful reconstruction is typical from as few as two or three images while over a hundred is still usable, so the input count has a knee worth locating rather than a monotone benefit.

title: Cacheability as an enumerated per-endpoint list
claim: Which endpoints may be cached is an explicit enumerated list rather than a predicate over request shape.

title: Does the emitter's span match the telemetry model
claim: The gateway emits OTLP spans directly, and the open question is whether the emitter's field set matches the corpus's token-usage-quadruple and server-owned-fields.

title: Third-party deployment numbers for security agents
claim: 2.6x correct patches (Chrome Security); +7.5-9.7% recall at 2.3-5.2x lower cost (Wiz); a critical vulnerability found in under 2 hours for work that usually takes months.

title: Count the longest run, not adjacent pairs
claim: The repetition check counts the longest run of identical shot sizes rather than equal adjacent pairs, and the code carries the corrected comment.

title: Cite numbers with the instrument's noise band
claim: Claims about a measurable class must cite numbers with the instrument's noise band, and a delta below the printed band is NO-FINDING: angle sigma about 24/len_px degrees, sub-0.25 m segments carry a +/-4 degree corner-bias floor, radii honest to about 3%, facet count +/-1; eyeball reads of these classes stopped counting as evidence.

title: A fixed diagnoser makes the loop not self-improving
claim: The diagnoser is fixed, so the loop is not self-improving in the sense the name claims.

title: Advisor-orchestrator bash hygiene
claim: The advisor orchestrator waits per pid and passes briefs via file rather than on the command line.

title: The lexical positive and near-miss trigger tier
claim: A trigger tier built from lexical positives and near misses, of which an earlier run adopted only the pairwise half.

title: Publication is a contamination surface
claim: A private fixed benchmark task, re-run per release and never published; the corpus owns freezing and discrimination, but nobody owns publication as a contamination surface.

title: Pin a vendored skill body by content hash
claim: A vendored skill is pinned in a lock file by computed hash, because an upstream edit to a prompt body changes behaviour with no version to notice it by.

title: Expected-failure marker expires itself when the bug is fixed
claim: `expectedFailure` runs the body and keeps artifacts; the suite goes red when the bug is fixed, so the marker cannot outlive its reason; distinct from skip.

title: Compose all matching rules strictest-of; no exception field
claim: Every matching rule is evaluated with level.max(), cap.min() and any deny, no early break; the config has no allow/except field, so an exception is unrepresentable and rule order cannot create a hole.

title: Fork scope is mandatory, with no default
claim: Fork scope has no default, no implicit main and no compatibility alias; a branch fork of a data-only branch is deliberately unavailable.

title: Report the first block that fails in execution order
claim: Patch validation reports the first failing block in execution order.

title: Audit both transports serving one contract
claim: One contract over two transports diverged on empty-array typing and honoured backpressure on one path only; control frames dropped on a lossy congestion path.

title: Enforce a record-size cap on encode and decode
claim: Enforce a record-size cap symmetrically so a record can never be written that the reader would later refuse.

title: A fuzzer portfolio: lab, hammer and performance mode
claim: The five-fuzzer taxonomy's remaining rows (idealized lab fuzzer, single-subsystem hammer, performance-mode whole-system run with realistic faults) may owe a portfolio technique.

title: Staged validation reliability multiplies
claim: Validation reliability compounds multiplicatively across staged validation (product of p_v), splitting syntactic (p near 1) from semantic/model-judged validation.

title: Bound the human-wait state or termination is unproven
claim: A plan with an unbounded human-wait state cannot be proven to terminate.

title: AI now authors about half of tracker issues
claim: AI authors about half of tracker issues, from 0 to about 50% in 18 months.

title: Non-engineers increasingly attach PRs
claim: Role blur: PM PR attachment rose from 3 to 10%, design from 1 to 8%.

title: Creative specificity as the targeting parameter
claim: The specificity of the creative is what selects the audience, so creative detail functions as a targeting parameter rather than as decoration.

title: One handle per asset, shared by the plan and the asset store
claim: Each asset gets one identifier that is identical in the planning document and the asset store, so a compiled prompt resolves references by name.

title: Creative direction grounded in demand data, not trend search
claim: One producer pulled platform analytics to choose a creative direction while the other ran a general trend search.

title: Artifact authored inside the boundary, trusted outside
claim: An artifact authored inside a trust boundary is consumed as trusted outside it, with no re-validation at the crossing.

title: At-most-once chosen because retry is dangerous
claim: The delivery posture is at-most-once, chosen deliberately because retrying the operation is more dangerous than losing it.

title: A per-target conversation split against one-mind-many-mouths
claim: The Slack adapter splits conversation state per target, which disagrees with the corpus's one-mind-many-mouths position on companion identity.

title: Explicit registries are the modal tool system at 34.3%
claim: Explicit registries are the modal tool system at 34.3% and protocol-based registration is still a minority at 14.3%, over a corpus frozen 2026-03-23.

title: A post-write hash guard mirrors the pre-write freshness gate
claim: A deterministic follow-up command rides the mutation call, guarded by a post-write hash, and is skipped rather than failed on interference; action fusion was eligible on 12.3 percent of cross-turn transitions with projected turns down 10.8 percent.

title: Three implementations of one measure, two contracts
claim: admission-control.ts truncates to the shorter vector while batch-dedup.ts and noise-prototypes.ts return 0 on a length mismatch, so a 384-dimension candidate against a 768-dimension row yields a plausible number in novelty scoring where the other two correctly refuse to answer.

title: An owning pointer handed to the terminal callback
claim: A weak-pointer handle that still owns the lifetime, with onClose(unique_ptr<Listener> self) making the destruction-order hand-off at the terminal callback explicit.

title: A data-placed debug thread-affinity guard
claim: A debug-only affinity assertion object placed on the data rather than in the functions that touch it, at zero release cost, catching cross-thread reads of a view snapshot.

title: A native-messaging browser host as an IPC contract
claim: A native-messaging browser host with select, detach and sync actions and per-browser manifest registration.

title: Three levels of done: call, tree, request
claim: Three levels of done - the call succeeded, the tree is consistent, the request was satisfied - illustrated by a refund API returning a struct instead of a bool with an 'if refund == true' caller a thousand lines away.

title: Branched import chains as a barrel-file signal
claim: Diamond and branched import chains are a measurable barrel-file signal, beside circular dependencies and cross-file re-export conflicts.

title: The content type is a hook, not a function of the extension
claim: resolveMimeType is a first-class plugin hook because browsers dispatch on the content-type header and a transform changes a file's language without changing its extension.

title: A process-local replay guard is an undeclared deployment constraint
claim: self.last_used_totp is in-memory, so two workers would each accept the same code once; correct for this tree's single-worker deployment and written down nowhere as a constraint.

title: Probe the capability ceiling from the initialized handler
claim: frames_maximum is obtained by calling the handler's update_default_settings({}) and reading sliding_window_size, falling back to sliding_window_defaults, then to the model-legal frame count nearest 97 computed from frames_minimum, frames_steps and frames_offset.

title: Provenance that reconstructs, not merely identifies
claim: The download URL of every adapter is written into the generation settings stored inside the video, so an output carries what is needed to reconstruct it rather than only to identify it.

title: Overlap frames are conditioning, not committed output
claim: A window's stated duration is its contribution; overlap frames are generated in addition and never counted.

title: Validate the window plan asymmetrically
claim: Overrun is reported with a predicted total, but only starvation (a later window receiving zero frames) is rejected.

title: Adaptive read-heads with a geometric ramp and mask invalidation
claim: A geometric prefetch ramp (base 16KB, x4, cap 16MB), ten heads per thread, invalidated by an atomic mask FETCH_OR'd with the file id.

title: Subdivide an upstream's coarse switch instead of choosing a side
claim: An 841-line carried patch whose whole substance is splitting one size-reduction macro into a finer-grained one, applied at build time.

title: A documentation defect files as a bug, in the bug-fix list
claim: The changelog files "corrected misleading documentation" - a landing page claimed a channel needed no configuration when it required a browser cookie - in the same list as a root-caused HTTP 400.

title: An optimisation with an off switch and a counter is a testable claim
claim: AST optimizer passes are switchable from the guest and print their statistics.

title: The eager arm as oracle, and the inverse round-trip as its other half
claim: The lazy-transform test peeks the pending affine and shape, applies, compares against the eager arm, then inverts both arms and compares again.

title: Skip on the infrastructure failure, by recognising its error strings
claim: Tests that need downloaded data skip via skip_if_downloading_fails, which recognises specific error strings so a real failure is not swallowed.

title: Dual-granularity export for machine readers
claim: Two generated machine-readable exports, an index and a full-content file, rather than one.

title: A second sighting for the two-channel feedback contract
claim: An inverted effect was only fixed once a screenshot was attached, in two separate builds.

title: Grandchildren hang you on the pipe, not the pid
claim: The non-interactive path closes output pipes on process exit so a detached grandchild cannot hang the agent waiting on pipe EOF, with a process-group SIGKILL on exit.

title: Explicit mentions read; ambient context only points
claim: An explicit file mention is rewritten into a synthetic read tool-call/result pair, so the model will not re-read it and compaction treats it as a tool result rather than a giant user message; ambient editor state is injected as a mention-only reminder, a pointer shape chosen with a stated revisit condition.

title: The tool set changes turn to turn
claim: Tools are re-registered every model round so installs take effect mid-turn, and the operating rule given to the model is never to assume a tool exists because it did earlier.

title: Rewind the world, fork the history, delete neither
claim: Rewind restores the filesystem and appends an event saying so; fork deep-copies history with provenance recorded inside the new log; the anti-loop argument is that an agent which rewinds can see what it already tried.

title: An unversioned install command makes the default branch a release channel
claim: A skill installed by the unversioned command tracks the latest stable release because that command installs from master, so the default branch is that file's release channel rather than its HEAD.

title: Cross-target lint from the development platform
claim: Cross-compile the other operating system target locally to catch compile-gated divergence before CI.

title: Evidence must live where the machine reads it
claim: A screenshot in the pull-request description is never read by the gallery that renders the entry, so the evidence has to be attached where the machine looks.

title: Dunning ladder versus entitlement state
claim: Is there a deliberate state where the customer owes money and still has access, and is its length a policy or a constant?

title: Zero inline retries with scheduled retry jobs as recovery
claim: The default is retry: 0 at the call site, with separately scheduled retry jobs as the real recovery path - the inverse of the usual queue posture.

title: An unmarked fallback is a quality regression with good uptime
claim: A gateway that silently swaps models produces a quality regression with excellent uptime numbers, which is harder to notice than an outage.

title: A percentage rollout samples uniformly from non-uniform risk
claim: Percentage rollout answers how many callers get the new version, not which ones, and the callers most likely to surface a regression are rarely a random sample.

title: Rollback latency ranks rollout mechanisms
claim: The alias and weighted-alias mechanisms are minutes and a flag is one toggle, so rank rollout mechanisms by how fast they roll back rather than by blast radius.

title: Review the method before it runs, not the result
claim: A monitoring agent read every method the model had in mind before it ran, to enforce constraints a result cannot reveal.

title: Job configuration frozen at enqueue
claim: The job's configuration is frozen when it is enqueued and carried with the job rather than read at run time.

title: An explicit commit point across four stores
claim: An index-done callback is the explicit commit point across all four stores.

title: What must be undone in the graph when a source is removed
claim: Deleting one document requires deciding what to undo in the graph built from it.

title: Seed assembly from the externally fixed element
claim: Seed a scene's assembly from the element whose dimensions are externally fixed rather than from the largest, because it becomes the scale reference and elements sized only relative to others cannot be placed first.

title: Workaround adoption is a prioritization signal
claim: Widespread adoption of a workaround is a prioritization signal and a process-failure symptom, not a violation to police: assigning blame to polyfills is like blaming car accidents on the ambulances.

title: Keep the unfair default-versus-default arm and label it
claim: A purposefully unfair benchmark arm is pedagogically useful and is kept and labelled rather than dropped; also, two structurally opposite corpora because they exercise disjoint code paths, and each arm's implicit environment pinned since one competitor takes Unicode behaviour from the locale.

title: Adversarial review by a different provider, defaulting to block
claim: An adversarial reviewer runs on a different provider, defaults to block on any error or ambiguity, and is prompted that its default assumption is that something was lost.

title: Reject before writing anything
claim: Rejections occur before artifacts or ledger records are written, so a refused run leaves no trace to clean up.

title: A handoff records dispatch outcome, not acceptance
claim: The handoff record states that the dispatch happened, not that the receiver accepted the work.

title: Run the worked example in CI, including its failures
claim: The worked example is executed on every CI run so it cannot quietly stop working, and two of its steps are things that should fail, shown failing.

title: Harness roles are not ranks
claim: Nothing infers a supervisor role from a brand name; harness roles are assigned, not ranked.

title: One major variable per experiment, versioned per run
claim: Evaluate a prompt revision separately from a model upgrade, and version prompt, model, dataset and configuration per run.

title: A stronger model may need a simpler prompt
claim: The prompt may be carrying complexity that comes from the model itself, so an upgrade can make its instructions redundant rather than merely make the suite easier.

title: Compose loops only from a closed gate catalog
claim: User-composed loops compile only from a closed catalog of seven built-in gates, with strict params, exclusive groups, and order mapped to a priority index times 10.

title: An agent induces the host's expensive precondition
claim: The agent triggered transcription of every clip, unasked, to satisfy a downstream request.

title: Sentinel-to-absence round-tripping at parse boundaries
claim: A sentinel value and an absent value must round-trip distinctly through parse and serialization boundaries.

title: Close an extension point when correctness depends on the implementer
claim: An extension point is closed rather than left open when correctness depends on the implementer, with a decision table for when.

title: Replication degrades to a remote call when provisioning fails
claim: When local provisioning fails, a replicating agent falls back to calling home to the machine it was spawned from.

title: Detached delegation is still process-local
claim: Background delegation is detached from the current turn but still process-local; work that must survive a process restart uses the scheduled or backgrounded-terminal path instead.

title: Usage-tracked auto-archival of agent-created skills
claim: Agent-created skills are auto-archived by usage, archived rather than deleted, and restorable.

title: Plugin settings are namespace-jailed with a read-only legacy fallback
claim: Plugin settings accept relative keys only, reject POSIX and Windows traversal both, and keep a legacy-subtree read fallback that writes never target.

title: Preflight external preconditions before the expensive build
claim: Bucket reachability, a signing key present in the keyring by fingerprint, branch, clean tree, upstream sync and CLI authentication are all checked before a cross-compile and a hardware sweep.

title: Test file ordering encodes an irreversible state cost
claim: A zz- filename prefix is load-bearing and says so: running last avoids a device reboot to clear in-memory rate-limit state.

title: Instrumented sync primitives behind a build tag
claim: Drop-in Mutex, Once and WaitGroup that log lock and unlock counts with caller file, line and function under a synctrace build tag, at zero cost otherwise.

title: The measurement boundary must contain the recovery loop
claim: A token saving measured per tool call can be a loss measured end to end: "We saved tokens locally and spent more globally."

title: External messages land as observations the agent may ignore
claim: External messages land as observations in the thought stream, and the agent decides if and when to respond.

title: A regressed rung is split, not retuned
claim: A tier that regressed on one hardware class was split into two tiers rather than retuned.

title: A human intermediary caps the agent multiplier
claim: The throughput multiplier requires the operator talking to agents directly; a human intermediary caps it.

title: Agents chaff-sort incoming changes before a human sees them
claim: Agents sort 400 incoming pull requests and validate them in a virtual machine so a human sees only merge-ready candidates.

title: The strongest model's plan is the handoff artifact
claim: One model ran out mid-job and another finished on its plan, and the same plan was re-run across five vendors.

title: Preload during the human's input lag
claim: An installer went from 42 minutes to 45 seconds by doing work during the human's input lag.

title: Transcode hostile codecs to proxies across preview, render, archive
claim: Media with hostile codecs is transcoded to proxies used across preview, render and archive, with an opt-out.

title: A model's default output converges on one house style
claim: A model's default UI output converges on one recognisable house style.

title: Gate synthesized motion by a replayed planning event
claim: Gate runtime-synthesized motion by a replayed planning event rather than by a clip.

title: Deployment smoothing sits outside the parity claim
claim: Label deployment smoothing as outside the parity claim - the client interpolates roots and SLERPs locals downstream of the compared boundary.

title: Plan with the strongest model, implement with a cheaper one
claim: Plan with the strongest model and implement with a cheaper one.

title: A public adapter so refusal is not exclusion
claim: A public adapter interface means an engine refused admission to the core can still ship, so refusal is not exclusion.

title: Resolution pinned by deadline, not by stage
claim: A real-time pipeline pins its one fidelity size by a latency deadline; resolution-as-stage-property prices a single-shot pipeline's one size by money and never by a latency budget.

title: A gate whose predicate is the human's comprehension
claim: The agent generates a quiz for you to make sure you correctly understand the changes before it opens a pull request.

title: Variance as the mean of squared deviations
claim: Compute variance as E[(x-mean)^2], never E[x^2]-mean^2, in float32 - the second form suffers catastrophic cancellation.

title: A runtime-only override never touches persisted settings
claim: Runtime-only overrides - command-line flags, an environment variable for an immutable install - never touch persisted settings.

title: A sparse payload needs system-enumerated obligations
claim: A sparse payload is safe only when the system enumerates the mandatory decisions - the assignment states the page's claim count and lists only the flagged ones.

title: On-demand escalation from counts to content
claim: A worker is handed counts and escalates to content on demand, scoped to the unit it owns.

title: An absent coverage record routes to full work
claim: An absent coverage record routes to full work, never to a skip.

title: A fallback that persists is uncorrectable
claim: Reject the unrecognized enum at the entry point, before any state write, because a fallback that persists is uncorrectable.

title: Provider default token caps and streaming-only empty 200s
claim: A framework's model metadata caps tokens by default, and a streaming-only gateway answers 200 with empty content.

title: Sweep the defect class from one instance
claim: Fix a host of strto*() bugs - the sweep-the-class-from-one-instance shape.

title: Generated fuzzers have curiously bad coverage
claim: Randomized and property-based generation dominates hand-written tests per unit of effort, and model-generated fuzzers have curiously bad coverage.

title: Wasted tool calls as an outcome dimension
claim: Unnecessary tool calls as an outcome dimension beside pass and fail - harness D solved it but used 40 unnecessary tool calls.

title: Time-of-day price constraints
claim: Price rows carry time-of-day constraints, claimed in the reference repository's README with the encoding not inspected.

title: A three-level eval hierarchy
claim: Assertions, a cadence, and A/B as three levels of one eval hierarchy.

title: Register as a per-surface user setting
claim: The control line's register axis, casual to formal, is exposed as product surface in the vendor's own app - is a per-surface register preference a voice-ux concern?

title: The rollup is the feature he built and does not use
claim: Quite honestly I almost never look at my daily brief - I like to go through the individual modules; later rebuilt as top-five-per-module.

title: The surface labels which mode produced it
claim: An assisted badge appears on the surface once a key is configured, so the surface declares which mode produced it.

title: One struct yields flags, validation and printable state
claim: Every config struct carries a Register/Validate/ToString triad, so command-line flags, validation and printable state all come from one struct.

title: Fallback composition across mounts with different capability levels
claim: One query's result is assembled from implementations with different capability levels, with the fallback safe to apply globally because it is a no-op over the native path.

title: Committed seed and hash-shard fallback for a duration-packed split
claim: Test shards are packed by measured duration with a committed seed, and hash-sharding as the fallback for tests with no history.

title: Learnings written from the agent's own failures at skill end
claim: At the end of a skill run, the agent writes learnings from its own failures back into the repo - operational self-improvement as a contribution rule.

title: Size-optimised mobile release profiles, measured
claim: Dedicated size-optimised build profiles for mobile releases, with the size measurement recorded in the PR that introduced them.

title: Flakiness as binary entropy over the pass rate
claim: A flakinessScore computed as binary entropy over the observed pass rate - 0 at either extreme, 1 at a 50% rate.

title: Three occurrences is the automation trigger
claim: Escalate skill -> reusable agent -> workflow on the third occurrence, and only for cost and scale.

title: A generated interface has a detectable house style
claim: Generated interfaces converge on a recognizable house style; when differentiation matters, descend an altitude. The interesting half is that the signature is detectable.

title: Meta-agent search shape: 3 candidates by 20 rounds
claim: The search ran 3 candidates over 20 rounds, cut to 1 candidate over 10 rounds for the expensive benchmark.

title: Selection halves elapsed time because proposal cost is fixed
claim: Selection reduces elapsed time by half because the proposal cost is fixed regardless of how many candidates survive.

title: The demo apps are all seam products
claim: Every showcase app is a seam product - first/last frame transition, camera-through-rooms, a draft comparison room - rather than an end-to-end generator.

title: Snapshot replicated state every N applied commands
claim: Snapshot the replicated state every N applied commands, to bound replay time on startup.

title: At scale, traceable beats abstracted
claim: Write the dumbest traceable code at scale; abstractions cost more than they save when the failure you will debug is a GC pause.

title: Software is evolved, and maintenance is unpriced
claim: Software is evolved rather than built, and maintenance is a fixed running cost the buyer does not price.

title: A failed enforcement is not self-describing
claim: Failed harnesses still needed a human to interpret the outcome: a blocked action that cannot explain itself is its own failure class.

title: Over-broad forbidden-command patterns
claim: Some forbidden-command patterns were too broad; the tuning was absorbed but the boundary was never checked against the corpus's execution-trust side.

title: An omitted ref retries because it has no row
claim: Batched triage over 12 postings uses local refs 1..N with 700-character excerpts, then deep-dives above a threshold with a per-run cap; a ref the model omits retries next run because it has no evaluation row.

title: Zero-item fan-out strands the join
claim: A fan-out with zero items strands the join and reports completed with an empty report.

title: Charge the budget for calls that were only requested
claim: Every requested tool call is charged to the budget and tools are removed from the surface at exhaustion.

title: A filename ingest key skips a same-name upload
claim: Ingestion is keyed on filename, so a second upload with the same name is skipped even when its content differs.

title: Density-biased routing by average top-k
claim: Database routing is decided by the average of top-k scores, which biases the choice toward the denser index rather than the more relevant one.

title: Session state written to a copy
claim: The store hands out copies, so writes to session state are written to a copy; the fix is to write through the event channel and re-fetch afterwards.

title: Shared-key timing and output-price-only cost
claim: Tool timing is measured under a shared key and cost is computed from output price only, so two different distortions land in the same report.

title: The video model cannot make a clip under 3-4 s
claim: The generative video model cannot produce a clip shorter than three to four seconds, which is the constraint that forced the half-speed-and-retime workaround.

title: Runtime portability broke, so the file forked
claim: The realtime handler exists twice, once per runtime, which is the one place runtime portability broke in a codebase that otherwise ships one build for the web-standard runtime subset.

title: SSRF on an operator-supplied base URL
claim: Custom-host validation guards an operator-supplied base URL, which is an SSRF surface introduced by an operator convenience.

title: An at-sentinel runner namespace with a shebang fallback
claim: Script runners are namespaced by an `@` sentinel, including a shebang-with-arguments fallback which is the interesting half.

title: A credit pre-check reserves the advertised ceiling
claim: The credit pre-check reserves the provider's advertised output ceiling rather than expected spend, so on a low balance every request can fail with a 402.

title: Advance the stamp on body change only
claim: Any body change including whitespace advances the provenance stamp, while front-matter changes do not.

title: Demo media disclosed as compressed for page speed
claim: The page discloses that its demo videos were compressed to optimize page performance - a claim about the artifact rather than about the model.

title: Golden-scenario replay with two eval modes
claim: Golden-scenario replay runs in deterministic and stochastic eval modes with a per-scenario tolerance.

title: A stub that reproduces the bug loudly
claim: A stub is designed so that an escaped call reproduces the bug loudly rather than passing vacuously.

title: Do not merge exclusion lists with different justifications
claim: Two exclusion lists that behave identically must not be folded together when their justifications differ, because folding them is the drift risk.

title: The delivery surface sets the top resolution rung
claim: Render at 720p for social upload because the platform re-encode hides the difference and it saves credits; nothing sets the top rung from the distribution surface.

title: Enumerate near-misses when text cannot be composited
claim: When a single-pass clip bakes in typography there is no compositing layer, so the prompt names the near-misses (not Dan with two Ns, not Dane).

title: Choose representation kind by what must be editable
claim: Split a scene: refinable meshes where editing is needed, a splat field for background that is only seen.

title: Some quality is settable only at generation
claim: Better topology is available through the refine option while generating, not afterwards.

title: Doc says first match wins; code composes strictest
claim: `docs/safety.md:29` says the first matching rule wins while the instrument composes the strictest of all matches, and the doc's next sentence contradicts it.

title: A capability the deployment lacks has no route
claim: When the deployment lacks a capability the route is not registered at boot, rather than guarded at runtime.

title: Blind rater identity, reveal after choice
claim: Human raters choose with model identity hidden and see it revealed after the choice, against brand bias.

title: A duration parser for a foreign format
claim: A 455-line duration format parser exists because the ecosystem's format is not the language's.

title: Exec-plugin credentials cross a trust boundary
claim: The exec-plugin path shells out to an operator-named binary for credentials; 4.0.0 changed it to accept yaml output.

title: Validate patches against the view the model saw
claim: A model patch is validated against the representation the model was shown, not the stored form.

title: Minimise a failing seed's input
claim: Recording, replaying and minimising a failing seed was named as an open question and not absorbed.

title: Automation lives in-repo, in the project language
claim: Automation lives in the same repo in the project's language; whoever can push to main can deploy; deployed version equals tip of main.

title: Grep the IR for the operation you avoid
claim: Compile to an intermediate representation and grep it for copies, because the IR is closer to source than assembly and target-independent; not productionized.

title: Terminal connection states outrank transient cooldown
claim: Terminal states (banned, expired, credits_exhausted) must never be overwritten by transient cooldown state.

title: Build upstream headers from scratch
claim: Correlation headers are never forwarded upstream; executors build upstream headers from scratch.

title: Compress tool output preserving failures and the tail
claim: Compression is an ordered multi-engine pipeline with command-class-aware filters that preserve failures, errors, changed files and the tail.

title: Keep failure history out of the retried step
claim: Keep failure history out of the retried step's context; readmit it only through a new plan version.

title: Make escalation order unskippable by precondition
claim: Enforce an escalation order through API preconditions, not documentation.

title: Do not use a static plan for exploratory tasks
claim: Static plans are wrong for exploratory, dynamic-goal and creative tasks.

title: Classify a patch four ways, including regressed
claim: Classify patch outcomes as fixed, regressed, still-failing and still-passing.

title: A generated docs page retired for hand-authored content
claim: The team that shipped an LLM-generated documentation page retired it for hand-authored static content.

title: Cleanup that must tolerate any state, and may throw
claim: The cleanup path must tolerate any state - the entry may be gone, the abort may have been called, the descriptor may have been closed - and unlike a destructor it may throw.

title: Per-queue-table as a design decision
claim: Every queue is its own physical table rather than rows in a shared table.

title: The tool registry is rebuilt every round
claim: The tool registry is rebuilt on every turn of the loop rather than assembled once per session.

title: Boundary-aware prefix lookup at token boundaries
claim: A prefix lookup for cached content is aligned to token boundaries rather than character boundaries.

title: Two-point schema validation: reject at install, skip at registration
claim: A schema is validated at two points with different postures - reject at install time, skip at registration time.

title: Simulate the constrained platform in the test double
claim: The test double simulates the constrained platform, and the measurement that produced the simulated constant is recorded in a comment beside it.

title: Token awareness makes memory an active control mechanism
claim: Reserving budget for future tool calls and subagents before assembling the prompt turns memory from passive storage into an active control mechanism.

title: Capability listings load within a budget of 1% of context
claim: The configuration audit lives at an in-session command while the same word in a shell prints only installation diagnostics, and installed-capability descriptions load within a listing budget defaulting to 1% of the context window.

title: Split design-system work: tokens versus implementation
claim: One tool decomposes an example or design file into reusable tokens, a coding agent then builds the technical design system and shared components, and the tokens are pushed back into the design tool.

title: Decompose a reference artifact into a written beat sheet
claim: Decompose a reference artifact into a written beat sheet and generate from the beat sheet rather than from the artifact.

title: Ask the skill library which of its own skills applies
claim: Rather than learning the library, ask it which of its own skills applies to the task at hand.

title: Video generation roughly ten times image cost per unit
claim: Video generation costs roughly ten times image generation per unit.

title: Label bot-authored notifications with the bot's name
claim: A digest or notification written by an agent is signed with the bot's name so the reader knows who is speaking.

title: Forked parser with a capped heap and ack backpressure
claim: Parsing runs in a forked child with a capped heap and streams per-session chunks back under ack-window backpressure, after out-of-memory failures on large log sets.

title: Source-tree applications for the whole design record
claim: Record this repository's architecture in the registry as source-tree applications for the whole design record, rather than only its corrections.

title: A second independent stack for llm-observability
claim: The bundle's subjects are largely single-stack and this tree is an independent implementation of trace ingestion, online scoring, price books and analytics storage, which would date several applications.

title: A guardrails service's dual image split
claim: The guardrails service ships two images - GPU by default with a CPU fallback, and a CPU-only multi-arch image for local and self-hosted deployment.

title: The repair ladder's long tail costs context
claim: Most files land inside ten attempts; the long tail took between fifty and a hundred, with prompts growing to 100,000 tokens and up to fifty related files pulled in as context.

title: Per-step inference cost of agent-driven CI
claim: 500 tests firing on every commit becomes a line item somebody will ask you about - the per-step inference cost of agent-driven CI is an operator-visible number.

title: Stand-in upstreams as released, versioned binaries
claim: Upstream stand-ins are released as versioned binaries on pinned ports, with a docker compose alternative, so local and CI runs exercise the same stand-in.

title: Absence needs its own prompt section
claim: Absence is not discoverable by reading, so the critic carries a 'what is missing' section with its own prompt, plus predict-before-reading and a pre-mortem.

title: Typechecking does not prove startup
claim: Declaration files accepted a peer range whose runtime lacked the API, so --help crashed before any provider loaded: a green typecheck is not evidence the program starts.

title: Virtual generation as the test substrate
claim: In-memory generation is the test substrate: the smoke lane parses the generated root manifest, and a separate curated build set installs and typechecks to prove compilation.

title: Wrapper functions for swappable globals
claim: Reference swappable globals through wrapper functions rather than directly, so a provider can be substituted without reaching every call site.

title: Codemods ship with the breaking change
claim: The migration codemods ship in the same release as the breaking change they migrate.

title: Per-finding-type truncation with an explicit remainder
claim: Truncate per finding type and carry an explicit remainder count - slice the first ten and print 'N more similar hints'.

title: A persistent module-graph session over a tool protocol
claim: Serve a persistent module-graph session over a language server or tool protocol instead of rebuilding the graph on every CLI invocation.

title: Probe the environment before using it
claim: Probe the environment before using it: verify POSIX tools exist, and read the lockfile to choose the package manager rather than assuming one.

title: Median 14 minutes to a first evidence-grounded report
claim: Median 14 minutes to a first evidence-grounded report, and 8x code per quarter with a named human owner per pull request.

title: Every stage commits an artifact the next stage reads
claim: Every stage commits an artifact the next stage reads, so the commit chain is the audit trail.

title: Records live in the filename, not a status key
claim: A record's state is carried by its path rather than by a status field inside it, so moving the file is the state transition.

title: A structured skip reason as the unavailable-action shape
claim: Every unavailability in the hook-chain mesh is rendered as a structured skip reason rather than as an error.

title: A banned-API test with a documentation-comment exemption
claim: A banned API is enforced by a source-scanning test that exempts comment lines, so the rule can be documented in the code it forbids.

title: A conditional suspend mode makes a section's posture unreadable
claim: A hook that suspends only when initialData is undefined gives a section a posture that cannot be read off the composition.

title: Reconciliation's memory price is unstated anywhere
claim: Reconciliation keeps the previous tree so unchanged subtrees can be cloned, and trades memory for that.

title: A prop manifest derived from one concept image
claim: The scene's asset list is derived from a single reference as a contact sheet, then generated in small batches.

title: An enclosed interior needs its own grade
claim: An interior takes a separate colour profile with overrides because the exterior's global grade does not carry inside.

title: Encode the mandatory tier in the type, not in a check
claim: In the bundle set the floor tier is a required field and the higher tiers are optional, so the floor cannot be omitted by construction.

title: A capability compiled, shipped, and deliberately not offered
claim: The highest tier is compiled and shipped but excluded from the default bundle set, with the comment that it is still experimental and the user must opt in explicitly.

title: One asset library, the same defect in two independent builds
claim: The same effect-inversion defect appeared in two independent builds drawing on one asset library.

title: Never ask the model to self-assess perceptible loss
claim: Test behaviour instead of asking the model whether compression lost anything, because there is a good chance it will just make something up.

title: Provider plugins by entry point with a community registry
claim: Model providers are discovered through packaging entry points and listed in a community registry rather than compiled into the library.

title: Planted-span benchmark for a text aligner
claim: A benchmark plants known spans in a document and times and checks the aligner against them, giving correctness and cost in one instrument.

title: Change control over translations with explicit conflict selection
claim: Translations are change-controlled with checkpoints and an explicit conflict-selection step rather than last-write-wins.

title: Needs checking and needs rewriting are two states
claim: A translation carries two distinct non-clean states - one meaning a human should verify it, one meaning it must be redone - and collapsing them loses the routing decision.

title: Document-level memory tiers with a self-writing glossary
claim: Translation memory is tiered by scope, including a run-scoped glossary that writes itself from the document being translated.

title: Declarative rule DSL and a signed rule-pack format
claim: Check rules are authored in a declarative DSL and shipped as a signed rule pack, which is the shape our anchors and checker rules would converge on if they merged.

title: Two normalization dialects for a sentence end
claim: A CJK stop mark is unambiguous, but an ASCII period needs a whitespace lookahead so "3.5" and "Mr. Smith" do not split a segment.

title: Role-specific models within one pipeline
claim: Extraction, summarisation and answering are separately configurable model roles, so the cheapest model clearing a stage's bar is a per-stage decision.

title: A parser plugin declares its parameters as schema
claim: A third-party parser ships a parameter schema the host validates before invoking it.

title: A drift gate from a self-describing artifact
claim: A special variable makes the completion function dump its own argument specs, which are diffed against the tool's own help output, and both sides assert non-empty before diffing.

title: Determinism costs the whole parallelism budget
claim: Sorting output will disable all parallelism, so ordering must be an opt-in that says what it costs.

title: Tiered-confidence classification into a two-level taxonomy
claim: A two-level wing and room taxonomy is populated by a classifier whose confidence is tiered by evidence kind: path 0.9, keyword 0.7, tag 0.6, pipeline 0.5, fallback 0.1.

title: Renders that carry their own recipe
claim: A vendor's first-party example corpus ships renders that carry the parameters that produced them.

title: Duration is derived from the control script and quantized
claim: The runner infers the output length from the action durations, and valid lengths follow 1 + 24m.

title: The prompt enhancer is mandatory on one path and forbidden on the other
claim: Long-video generation strongly recommends running through the prompt enhancer while the causal path passes captions verbatim and does not invoke it.

title: Unscoped handlers still run beside the active mode
claim: One mode scope decides at a time, but unscoped handlers still run beside the active mode, and the plugin API cannot set scope.

title: Two camera beats in one reference clip
claim: One reference-driven clip carries two camera beats.

title: Agent demand forces the automation surface to grow
claim: Agent popularity is expected to keep growing the host application's scripting API.

title: A swarm substitutes for continuous learning
claim: Context and environment improve while weights stay fixed, so a population of agents works around the absence of continuous learning.

title: Authority as an unforgeable value, not a boolean parameter
claim: Authority is passed as an unforgeable value rather than as a boolean parameter a caller can set.

title: Co-developed units resolve a shared requirement once
claim: Units developed together resolve a shared requirement once rather than each resolving it separately.

title: A capacity class boundary needs a tolerance
claim: A nominal 16GB device reports 15.7-15.9 after driver reservation, so the class boundary is 16.0 - 0.5, and the tree states no bound on what the tolerance misclassifies downward.

title: One content-free telemetry line per pass plus a reader
claim: Micro-compaction telemetry is one content-free JSON line per pass carrying only counts, with a report script that turns a log into an answer.

title: Red-green verify a regression test
claim: Revert the fix, confirm the test goes red, restore - a test that passes against the buggy code does not protect against regression.

title: Brains and hands: the model drives a disposable VM
claim: The model runs on the coordinator and manipulates a disposable virtual machine, so untrusted contribution content cannot contaminate it.

title: A compile-bound engine slows the agent's loop
claim: A compile-bound engine slows agent iteration loops.

title: Hand the agent a repository URL and say install it
claim: Hand the agent a repository URL and say install it.

title: Upsampling a generator's native rate in the consumer

Our not-better rows and untriaged tables carry a return condition only sometimes, and LESSONS entries never. A/B: take the last 40 not-better and untriaged rows; arm A as written, arm B with a return condition added by a fresh worker from the row's own evidence; measure, over the later history already on main, how many of each arm's rows were re-derived by a later run without reading the earlier verdict (the waste the condition prevents) and how many conditions in B had already fired unnoticed. Deterministic: git log over sources and applied.md, matched by technique slug and claim.

title: An unreadable sibling record fails the board check instead of reading as clear
claim: The run board skips any run record it cannot parse, so an unreadable sibling reads as no sibling: a silent false clear, the failure its own header names as the worst it can have. The source's guard and build slots refuse on unreadable state and allow only on absent state. A/B: seed a corrupt and a mid-rename sibling record into a scratch board; arm A (current) claim/check exit 0 over a held subject, arm B counts unreadable records and exits 1 (instrument failed). Also measure whether a read racing the temp-then-rename publish ever fails on this host (premise unmeasured: 1,000 concurrent publish/read pairs). Floor: no change for readable boards.

title: beat --subject checks contention and grants only the clear tokens
claim: beat --subject/--path adds claims with no conflict check and outside the claim gate that bdb7dbf2 put around claim; doctrine leaves the follow-up check to memory. The source grants the clear paths, refuses and names the contended ones in one reply. A/B: rebuild every beat --subject/--path call from transcripts (as the lease replay on branch ab/lease-guard-replay does) and count calls whose token touched a live sibling's claim, and how many were followed by a check before the first write. Arm B replays a partial-grant beat over the same calls. Zero silent overlaps means hygiene only; any non-zero is a live hole.

title: Board liveness from evidence the run leaves, not only its own beat
claim: Board liveness reads the run's self-report (beat < 45 min or a fresh lock), which goes stale while the run waits on builders; memory records a claim reaped mid-run. The source refuses a forced release while any of four activity signals is fresh, a sibling app reads transcript growth, and every acting call refreshes last-active. A/B over recorded transcripts and scratch dirs: arm A current runLiveness; arm B adds transcript or --scratch growth within 45 min and counts every --run board call (check, lock) as a beat; unlock --force runs the same evidence judgement. Target: run-minutes reported dead while the transcript grew; floor: run-minutes reported live after the session ended must not rise.

title: A broken lock's holder learns it before the guarded write
claim: A holder whose commit/ledger lock was broken past its TTL is never told and proceeds to the guarded write. A fleet task relay stamps every lease with a fence each later write must match, and a refused renewal stops the run without delivering. A/B on the stale-lock harness behind breakIfUnchanged: holders sleep past the TTL before writing; arm A current lock, arm B a lock verify against the acquire fingerprint immediately before the write. Target: trials where a broken holder still wrote (A expected > 0, B must be 0).

title: Refuse a claim token broader than a subject
claim: Nothing stops --path . or --subject <bundle>, which with the prefix fold contends with every sibling. The source moved over-broad reservation patterns from a warning to a refusal after warnings did not stop them. A/B: replay every claim/beat token in retained transcripts; count tokens shallower than a subject and the sibling claims each would have contended with; arm B refuses them. Floor: no legitimate subject-level claim refused.

title: A code-mode row names the commit as it landed on its durable branch, not the pre-rebase sha

All whole in frame. Nothing else in the room. No text.' A fresh pre-read seat, paths only, answers yes or no per object: present, whole in frame, on the floor. render.instrument: render.discrimination, render.stopRule, render.repairRule and render.critic are part of this instrument and were fixed before any measurement.
