Operator blind pick per pair decides; both pairs are answered together. B on both: better. B on front and A on side-high: the first half stands and the held-out half of the claim is false, so a scoped amendment. A on front: not-better. Tie or neither per render-proof. Bank rules per gpu-bank: lease through hold.py for the proof's life, ComfyUI's queue only, no recycle and no /free, foreign work stops at a boundary. Submit consistency.py's flux_workflow graph through the queue; do not use flux_still.py, which can recycle ComfyUI. Critic and builder are one family (Claude), n=1 per arm plus one unshown replicate: record both on the row. Every step runs without a person; the only human step is the pick afterwards, which waits on the review page. It cannot show a real photo as anchor, a solved camera, or a mesh-level fix: the row tests assembly only. Rounds of shift-rjf-1 are design evidence and are not arms.
render.discrimination: Fixed now, per view, both views required, floor 1.5x as DISCRIMINATION_RATIO. between = sheet_distance of R0 against arm B's final still. within = sheet_distance of arm B's final still against b2's final still, where b2 is a second full run of the same three-round loop from the same R0 with its own fresh seats, run after B and never shown. Agent-authored arms take a replicate floor per render-proof, drawn from the treated arm because the critic is what conditions layout. No minimum over intermediate rounds, and no intermediate distance enters the gate; they may be recorded, never used. Reassembling R0 once must measure 0.0 on both views (it did on shift-rjf-1), or the floor is void. A view below 1.5x refuses the whole proof: no pick, no post-hoc pair, the row goes unmeasurable with its numbers, and a further design is the operator's call.
render.stopRule: Exactly three rounds per replicate. No early stop on a high score, no fourth round, no choosing a better earlier round. Seats per replicate: four critics (the fourth scores the final still and produces no fix) and three builders. Order: reference, R0, arm B, b2, then held-out renders of R0, B and b2, then distances, then seal. Budget stop 30 GPU min at a job boundary, summed as in shift-rjf-1: keep everything, stay held, record progress. A restart skips jobs already in results.jsonl.
render.repairRule: No mesh runs in the loop, because the claim is a fix to the build script only, and 35.8 of shift-rjf-1's 36.9 GPU min and its scripted stand-ins followed from re-meshing. A critic finding about a mesh's own shape is logged as a cap this row cannot move. layout.json may hold, for exactly these four objects: x, y, yaw, width, depth, height in metres (0.2 to 3.0) and a colour gain (0.5 to 2); z is floor contact, computed by build.py. A validator runs before each render. A failed round (invalid layout, seat error, Blender exit, missing still, a mesh that fails to import) stays in the record, counts toward the three, is not re-run, and the next round starts from the last valid layout. These void the arm, with no repair: any changed sha of build.py, a GLB or the reference; any added, hidden, deleted or vertex-edited object; a scripted stand-in for a generated object; no valid round after R0. A void arm B or b2 ends the run blocked with no pick. A failed R0 does too.
render.critic: A fresh seat per round, given paths only: reference, a neutrally named front.png in its own folder, and the frozen four-object list with the 0-10 anchors from shift-rjf-1. It is told no round number, score history, goal or builder report. It never sees side-high: no side-high file exists until every round of both replicates is frozen, and no seat is spawned after that. Its score is same-family under a-judge-of-the-generators-family-is-not-independent: a filter that drives fixes, read beside the pick (per-round totals, whether the final total rose, whether it agrees with the pick), never the verdict, a stop condition or a selector.
render.falsifiable: Round 0 of shift-rjf-1 carried a flat plant and a panel-shaped barrel, so any change looked like a gain. Here both arms hold the same sound meshes and a competent first pass, so only layout and colour gain can move. The loop can lose four ways: the operator picks one pass on front; a fix fitted to the front (depth, depth-axis scale, yaw of the 0.14-deep door, all hard to see from there) reads wrong on side-high and loses that pair; two loops land too far apart for their move from R0 to clear 1.5x, which refuses the proof; or a same-family critic moves a good layout away from the reference while its score rises.

That runner hash is uncommitted work: committed HEAD reads a `prompt` field no frame here has, and fails on any end frame. Any other hash stops the row, held, with a line saying so. Runner traps, all handled below: seed is base + index of the id in sorted(keyframes), so arm folders keep identical id sets; output goes to <arg>/music-clip/clips, so pass the arm's folder and never the operator's; it waits on a busy queue instead of stopping, so run one clip at a time with --only and re-read the queue between clips, and if anything else appeared stop at the boundary and stay held. Re-check the 0.96 against the direct chain within 2.0, or stop. Same look, same file, on every arm.

render.instrument: Blind pick per shot with render-triage sheet, no --allow-indistinct, and the ungraded existing clip as manifest.showcase. The operator's pick is the verdict. Beside it, never the verdict: mean RGB of first and last frame against the graded key; and pixel distance, which is expected to be large. Mapping: b on every shot is better, a measured amendment to 'The import is also the lever' in generated-shot-sourcing, and the look file's stage is the key. a on every shot is not-better, a boundary amendment there, and the stage is the cut. Split is a scoped amendment by shot kind.
render.discrimination: Fixed now, per shot, floor 1.5x. A pixel distance cannot work: two seeds differ in motion, and the question is colour. Colour distance: per frame a 32-bin histogram per RGB channel, normalised, L1 summed, mean over 124 matched frames. Seed control from the treated arm: b at --seed 6000, three more clips. between = a against b. within = b against its seed control. What each result means, written first: under 1.5x on a shot means the two routes land within seed noise in colour, so nobody is asked; the row records that the grade survived the model to that precision, which is a dated figure and not a preference, and it stays unmeasurable. At or over 1.5x, the pair is shown. The existing clips were rendered before this row, so they are not proven reproducible at their seed; colour distance is insensitive to a small motion change, and the pixel distance is recorded beside it for that reason.
render.falsifiable: b loses if the video VAE or the model moves the look off the table, if highlights in the blast clip shift differently from the table, or if a cut grade's exact per-frame hold simply reads better. a loses if a table over finished clips looks laid on top while the conditioned clip looks shot that way.
render.stopRule: Exactly 6 clips. A failed clip is recorded and retried once. No second look, no tuning of the table after any clip exists.
